name: TB Memory Pools & the Optical Fabric

pages.text: $(bold)Since 0.6.1 compute blades carry no memory at all.$() A blade is pure compute; memory moves into dedicated cabinets. That is not robbing Peter to pay Paul — it puts two costs on two meters: compute is bought in CWU/t, memory in TB.$(br2)A $(item)VRAM Storage Rack$() has 4 HBM slots:$(li)$(item)IV HBM Module$() — $(bold)4 TB$() each, $(bold)16 TB$() fully loaded;$(li)$(item)LuV HBM Module$() — $(bold)16 TB$() each, $(bold)64 TB$() fully loaded.

pages.title: The 5×5×3 Memory Rack
pages.text: $(li)$(#0E7490)Layer y=0$(): the full $(item)VRAM Rack Casing$() plinth; the energy and maintenance hatches ride this layer.$(li)$(#0E7490)y=1..3$(): the module bays behind $(item)Reinforced Glass$() doors, with a $(item)Computer Casing$() memory spine at the back.$(li)$(#0E7490)Layer y=4$(): a $(item)Tungstensteel Frame$() cable tray.$(li)$(#0E7490)Controller$(): front face, second layer, $(bold)(2, 1, 0)$().$(br2)Memory only counts while $(bold)online$(): pull a module, leave maintenance unfixed, pause with a soft mallet or cut the power and that cabinet's TB leaves the pool at once — anything loaded into it unloads the same tick.

pages.title: Training gates follow the target model
pages.text: $(bold)Since 0.6.2 the pretraining cluster's OOM gate is validated against the target model selected on its screen$(), no longer a flat 96 TB:$(li)$(bold)Qwen 9187 Pro-Max-Ultra$(): 96 TB / 32 CWU/t (one LuV + two IV racks lands exactly on it; two full LuV racks clear it)$(li)$(bold)DeepSeek-V6767 Flash$(): 64 TB / 24 CWU/t (one full LuV rack)$(li)$(bold)DeepSeek-V6767 Pro$(): 128 TB / 48 CWU/t (two full LuV racks)$(li)$(bold)GLM-2333 Flash$(): 32 TB / 16 CWU/t (two IV racks)$(li)$(bold)GLM-2333 Max$(): 80 TB / 32 CWU/t (one LuV + one IV rack)$(br2)The bigger the family, the more TB and CWU/t it needs; short on either and training $(bold)refuses to start$() with an explicit OOM / compute reason instead of collapsing mid-run.$(br2)$(bold)Switching target clears the checkpoint$(): one family's weights cannot resume another's run.

pages.title: Optical Fabric Switch: Many Cabinets, One Pool
pages.text: Loose cabinets do not make a cluster. The $(item)Optical Fabric Switch$() aggregates every compute and memory rack within $(bold)16 blocks$() into one pool:$(li)each IV air-cooled rack contributes $(bold)24 CWU/t$();$(li)each LuV liquid-cooled rack contributes $(bold)64 CWU/t$();$(li)the memory cabinets' TB is summed for the router and the training cluster.$(br2)It is also a $(bold)hard ceiling$(): demand above $(bold)128 CWU/t$() in one tick trips $(bold)503 Server Busy$() for a $(bold)15-second (300-tick)$() cooldown, during which nobody is served.

pages.title: The 5×4×3 Backplane Cabinet
pages.text: $(li)$(#0E7490)y=0$(): the heavy backplane plinth with the energy and maintenance hatches.$(li)$(#0E7490)y=1$(): the port row, controller front-centre at $(bold)(2, 1, 0)$().$(li)$(#0E7490)y=2$(): the exposed fibre tray behind $(item)Reinforced Glass$().$(li)$(#0E7490)y=3$(): a $(item)Steel Frame$() overhead bridge.$(br2)The GUI reports member count, aggregated CWU/t, aggregated TB and the remaining 503 cooldown.
